findings.fix: Remove `user-scalable=no` (and any `maximum-scale` restriction) so users can zoom.
findings.violation: `user-scalable=no` disables pinch-to-zoom, which violates WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text) and harms low-vision users.

findings.evidence: `style="color:#999999"` on "Passengers should review the updated schedule at any station kiosk."
findings.fix: Remove the inline color override or use a darker color (e.g., #595959 or the default body text color) that meets 4.5:1 contrast.
findings.violation: Light gray (#999999) text on a white background yields roughly a 2.85:1 contrast ratio, failing the WCAG AA minimum of 4.5:1 for normal text.

findings.evidence: "Passengers should review the updated schedule at any station kiosk." and "Local residents may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app." both appear under the heading "Accessibility improvements," and both end with the identical sentence "Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Replace both paragraphs with content that actually describes accessibility improvements, and remove the duplicated sentence.
findings.violation: Neither paragraph discusses accessibility, and the repeated closing sentence suggests reused boilerplate filler rather than content relevant to the section heading.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals through the mobile app. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Rewrite the second sentence to describe what actually happens after checking arrivals, or delete it.
findings.violation: Checking real-time arrivals isn't a "request" that produces a confirmation message, so the second sentence doesn't logically follow the first - indicating mismatched template text.

findings.fix: Add a `<caption>` such as "Zone status" as the first child of the table.
findings.violation: The table has no accessible name describing its purpose, making it harder for screen reader users to understand what the table represents when navigating by table.

findings.fix: Change the first cell of each data row to `<th scope="row">`.
findings.violation: "North" and "South" act as row headers but are marked up as plain `<td>` cells instead of `<th scope="row">`, reducing navigability for screen reader users.

findings.evidence: "Passengers may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app. The change takes effect on the following service day."
findings.fix: Replace with content describing actual weekend service changes, or move this paragraph to the fares section.
findings.violation: This content is about fare adjustments, not weekend service, and is unrelated to the section heading.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can report a service issue by calling rider services. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Replace with weekend-service-specific content or relocate to a more relevant section.
findings.violation: This content, about reporting service issues, is also unrelated to the "Weekend service" heading.

findings.fix: Replace with a responsive rule such as `max-width:960px; width:100%`.
findings.violation: A fixed pixel width will overflow small/mobile viewports and, combined with `user-scalable=no` in the viewport meta tag, traps users unable to zoom out to see the clipped content.

findings.evidence: `style="height:60px;overflow:hidden"` on an element with `role="status"` containing two sentences of text
findings.fix: Remove the fixed height/overflow clipping, or use `min-height` so the box grows to fit its content.
findings.violation: The fixed height with clipped overflow can visually truncate the status message for sighted users, even though screen readers (via the live region) receive the full text - an inconsistent experience.

findings.fix: Darken the border color to one meeting at least 3:1 contrast, e.g., #767676.
findings.violation: The border color #9d9d9d against a white background has roughly a 2.5:1 contrast ratio, below the WCAG 1.4.11 minimum of 3:1 for UI component boundaries.

findings.evidence: `<div class="icon-delete" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol">`
findings.fix: Replace with `<button type="button" aria-label="Delete item">` containing the icon.
findings.violation: A non-interactive `<div>` simulates a button via ARIA/tabindex instead of using a native `<button>`, losing built-in keyboard activation (Enter/Space) semantics.

findings.evidence: Three `<div class="step">` elements ("Choose a plan", "Enter payment details", "Confirm your order") with no list or state markup
findings.fix: Mark the steps up as an ordered list and add `aria-current="step"` to the active step, or include visually hidden "Step X of 3" text.
findings.violation: The multi-step wizard has no semantic structure (list) or indication of which step is current, so assistive technology users can't tell how many steps exist or where they are.

findings.evidence: "For the full list of upcoming adjustments, `read the accessibility improvements list`."
findings.fix: Change the link text to something accurate, such as "view the full list of upcoming adjustments."
findings.violation: The link text "read the accessibility improvements list" doesn't match the surrounding sentence about "upcoming adjustments" or its `/fares/history` destination, which is misleading, especially out of context (e.g., for screen reader users browsing a links list).
The label's `for` attribute ("topic-alt") doesn't match the select's `id` ("topic"), so clicking the label won't focus the control and screen readers won't announce the association.

findings.evidence: `<label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label">Phone number (required)</label>` next to `<input id="phone" type="tel" autocomplete="tel">`
findings.violation: The label text states the field is required, but the input has no `required` or `aria-required="true"` attribute, so the requirement isn't programmatically enforced or announced.

findings.evidence: `<input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true">` with `<span class="error-text" aria-live="polite" id="s3-form-promo-error">`
findings.fix: Default to `aria-invalid="false"` (or omit it) and toggle it on validation, and add `aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error"` to the promo input.
findings.violation: `aria-invalid="true"` is hardcoded in the static markup, so the field is announced as invalid before the user has entered anything, and the error text isn't linked via `aria-describedby`, so screen reader users aren't told why it's invalid.
